LIM_9_infinite_self_check_recursion_risk.where: process-level (not code-level), discovered in Rounds 7-10 of M1.8 self-check
LIM_9_infinite_self_check_recursion_risk.issue: After Round 6 sealed CODE-layer self-check, Rounds 7-9 each found NEW errors in the worktree-save commit just made by the previous round (description-layer cross-file inconsistencies in .context state files). Each round's fix introduces a new round-N+1's target — risk of infinite recursion at progressively smaller granularity (value → context → attribution → meta-description)
LIM_9_infinite_self_check_recursion_risk.blast_radius: TIME — each description-layer round costs ~5min but finds at most 2-3 cosmetic/attribution issues with zero functional impact. By Round 10 the marginal value is descriptive-only
LIM_9_infinite_self_check_recursion_risk.fix: Define a HARD STOP rule: when self-check rounds shift from finding code-bugs to finding only description-layer issues (numerical typos / attribution drift / cross-file phrasing inconsistency), declare SEALED at the next round and stop. New rounds may only be opened on (a) user reports actual functional bug or (b) downstream consumer breaks. State files are documentation, not specs — they describe the truth in git, they don't define it
LIM_9_infinite_self_check_recursion_risk.fix_when: ALREADY APPLIED at Round 10 of M1.8 self-check (this very lesson). Future milestones M2a+ inherit this rule
LIM_9_infinite_self_check_recursion_risk.introduced_in: Implicit in self-check methodology since M1.5; first explicitly observed Rounds 7-10 of M1.8

LIM_8_runner_protocol_docstring_drift.fix_summary: Rewrote docstring with 4 explicit contract clauses: (1) RUNNING(progress=0.0) is OWNED BY entrypoint, handlers MUST NOT re-mark; (2) RUNNING(progress>0.0) is handler-owned for milestone reports; (3) DONE handlers SHOULD self-mark, entrypoint has defensive safety net; (4) FAILED entrypoint catches all exceptions, handlers MAY self-mark for richer context but not required. Plus added 4 reverse-assertion contract tests to test_runner.py: test_entrypoint_marks_running_before_handler_invoked + test_entrypoint_catches_failed_when_handler_does_not_self_mark + test_entrypoint_defensive_done_safety_net_when_handler_silent + test_entrypoint_preserves_handler_progress_reports. Per Round 4 lesson: positive+negative test pairs prevent condition-widening regressions in future entrypoint refactors.

LIM_10_test_runner_isolation_via_load_st.issue: test_stage_entrypoint_marks_done_on_success registers a lambda for INGEST stage, then calls _stage_entrypoint, but entrypoint internally calls _load_stage_modules() which imports autoclip.pipeline.ingest, which calls register_stage_handler(INGEST, run_ingest) overwriting the test's lambda (last-wins). When run as `pytest tests/unit/test_runner.py` standalone, the test FAILS (real run_ingest is invoked, raises IngestError because raw/ dir is missing). When run as part of `pytest tests/` (full suite), it PASSES — likely because some other test's import order or monkeypatch happens to leave the lambda in place. This is a pre-existing test isolation bug from M1.4, NOT introduced by LIM#8 fix.
LIM_10_test_runner_isolation_via_load_st.blast_radius: low — only the standalone test_runner.py invocation pattern is affected; CI runs the full suite which passes; developers running single-file pytest may see false negatives
LIM_10_test_runner_isolation_via_load_st.fix_options: (a) make _clean_handlers fixture re-clear handlers AFTER _load_stage_modules runs, (b) add a test-only env var to skip _load_stage_modules in entrypoint, (c) refactor entrypoint to accept handler-source as injectable parameter. Option (b) is cheapest; option (c) is cleanest
LIM_10_test_runner_isolation_via_load_st.fix_when: M2a kickoff or whenever first developer notices the standalone-failure mode
